subjectSummary.answer: AMD designs and sells processors, graphics products, and other computing products. In the nine months ended September 26, 2026, its largest reportable segment was Data Center, with $21.0 billion in revenue. [The 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/) reports strong demand for EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs as the main driver of that segment’s growth.

recentMaterialEvents.claim: For the third quarter ended September 26, 2026, Data Center revenue was $8.546 billion, up 97% from the same quarter a year earlier, driven mainly by demand for EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs. [10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/)
AMD’s Q3 2026 results report record Data Center revenue and the launch of Instinct MI450 Series GPUs. [AMD Q3 results](https://ir.amd.com/)

A November 3, 2026 Reuters report said AMD forecast 2027 revenue growth above 80% and fourth-quarter 2026 revenue of about $17 billion, plus or minus 3%. These are company forecasts reported by Reuters. [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/)

factLedger.claim: AMD reported $35.166 billion in revenue for the nine months ended September 26, 2026. [10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/)
Data Center revenue for the nine months ended September 26, 2026 was $21.039 billion, up 87% from the same period in 2025. [10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/)
Client and Gaming revenue for the nine months ended September 26, 2026 was $11.168 billion, up 5% from the same period in 2025. [10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/)
Embedded revenue for the nine months ended September 26, 2026 was $2.959 billion, up from $2.504 billion in the same period in 2025. [10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/)
AMD reported that no customer accounted for at least 10% of consolidated revenue in fiscal years 2025 and 2024. [10-K](https://www.sec.gov/)

whatItDoes.answer: AMD makes server processors and accelerators for data centers, processors and graphics products for personal computers and gaming, and embedded computing products. Its 10-Q describes these product groups under Data Center, Client and Gaming, and Embedded. [10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/)

howItMakesMoney.answer: For the nine months ended September 26, 2026, AMD reported revenue of $21.039 billion from Data Center, $11.168 billion from Client and Gaming, and $2.959 billion from Embedded. These are segment revenue amounts; the supplied evidence does not provide revenue shares for this period. [10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/)

customers.answer: No customer accounted for at least 10% of AMD’s consolidated revenue in fiscal years 2025 or 2024, according to its 2025 10-K. The supplied 2026 10-Q excerpt does not state whether that remained true for 2026. [10-K](https://www.sec.gov/)

geography.answer: The supplied 2026 10-Q evidence does not give revenue amounts or shares by geographic region. [10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/)

purchaseRecurrence.answer: The filings describe several product markets and report seasonal revenue patterns, but the supplied evidence does not explain how often customers repurchase AMD products. [10-K](https://www.sec.gov/)

pricingPower.answer: The 2025 10-K reports that Client revenue rose partly because processor average selling prices increased 15% in 2025. This is evidence of higher prices in that business during that year; the supplied evidence does not establish whether AMD can keep raising prices. [10-K](https://www.sec.gov/)

recessionCyclicality.answer: AMD says the semiconductor industry is highly cyclical and has experienced severe downturns. It also says demand depends partly on conditions in the industries its products serve, and that its results vary by quarter and season. [10-K](https://www.sec.gov/)

managementTrackRecord.answer: AMD’s filings identify Lisa Su as chair and chief executive officer in the supplied earnings report. The supplied evidence does not provide a detailed record of management’s past guidance against results. [AMD Q3 results](https://ir.amd.com/)

capitalAllocation.answer: AMD completed its acquisition of ZT Systems in March 2025 for $3.2 billion in cash and 8.3 million shares of common stock. The supplied evidence does not provide a fuller account of capital allocation decisions. [10-K](https://www.sec.gov/)

companyKpis.answer: For the nine months ended September 26, 2026, Data Center revenue was $21.039 billion and operating income was $6.584 billion; Client and Gaming revenue was $11.168 billion and operating income was $1.730 billion; Embedded revenue was $2.959 billion and operating income was $1.177 billion. AMD reported total revenue of $35.166 billion and total operating income of $6.298 billion for that period. [10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/)

riskFactors.answer: AMD lists intense competition, semiconductor industry downturns, changing demand in customer industries, delays or shortcomings in product launches, loss of a major customer, economic uncertainty, seasonal results, and risks to protecting its technology as potential risks. [10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/)

The increase in operating income was primarily due to higher revenue, partially offset by higher cost of sales, approximately $440 million of net inventory and related charges associated with the U.S. government export control on AMD Instinct™ MI308 Data Center GPU products and higher operating expenses. sources.summary: AMD Q3 2026 highlights relevant to AI semiconductor market demand, supply constraints, and Helios MI450 developments: - Financials and growth: Q3 2026 revenue reached a record level, with Data Center segment up 97% year-over-year to $8.5B, driven by strong demand for AMD Instinct GPUs and EPYC processors. Client/Gaming was down 8% overall; Embedded rose 29%. - Data Center demand and products: Surge in data-center demand centered on AMD Instinct MI450 Series GPUs and 6th Gen AMD EPYC CPUs. The Data Center segment nearly doubled YoY, signaling robust AI/ML workload adoption. - Helios and MI450 deployment: AMD reiterates expectations for accelerating growth in Q4 as it scales Helios and Venice production. Recent deployments include: - Helios rack-scale systems powering workloads at Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, using Instinct MI450 GPUs and 6th Gen EPYC CPUs. - HPE/Vultr collaboration to deploy AMD Helios by HPE systems. - Oracle Cloud Infrastructure rolling out OCI Compute E7 instances with 6th Gen EPYC CPUs.
sources.snippet: AMD delivers record quarter as Data Center segment revenue grows 97% year-over-year, driven by record sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs ... “We delivered a record quarter with revenue exceeding the high end of our guidance as Data Center segment sales nearly doubled year-over-year,” said Dr. Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO. “Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continued to strengthen, and we expect growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and ‘Venice’ production. With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years.” ... Segment Summary - Data Center segment revenue was a record $8.5 billion, up 97% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for AMD EPYC™ processors and the launch of AMD Instinct™ MI450 Series GPUs. - Client and Gaming segment revenue was $3.7 billion, down 8% year-over-year. Client business revenue was $2.9 billion, up 7% year-over-year, driven by sales of AMD Ryzen™ mobile processors.

sources.title: AMD forecasts quarterly revenue above estimates as data-center growth accelerates By Reuters
sources.summary: Summary: - AMD projects rapid 2027 growth, with overall revenue up more than 80% driven largely by data-center chips (about 80% of next year’s sales). CEO Lisa Su emphasized data-center, CPU, and data-center AI demand as key growth drivers. - Data-center revenue surged 97% year over year to a Q3 record of $8.55 billion; Q4 revenue guidance around $17 billion (±3%), topping consensus about $16.23 billion. - AMD is expanding AI product lines beyond standalone chips, including the Helios rack system (MI455X accelerator + Venice server chips) in production and entering broader AI workloads to compete with Nvidia. - Meta is testing the initial Helios systems; the ramp-up is expected in Q4. - The sector faces a global memory shortage for high-bandwidth memory used in AI processors, affecting supply as manufacturers increase production. Key context for your query: - November 2026 developments align with AMD’s stronger-than-expected data-center demand and AI-focused product rollout (Helios/MI450 era, Venice chips) as it competes with Nvidia. - Helios MI455X + Venice server chips form AMD’s rack-scale system to capture more AI workloads in data centers.
sources.snippet: Nov 3 (Reuters) - AMD forecast faster-than-expected 2027 growth as its data-center sales surge and its multibillion-dollar challenge to Nvidia gathers pace, sending its shares up 8% in extended trading. ... On a conference call with analysts, AMD CEO Lisa Su said the company expects overall revenue to rise more than 80% in 2027. Su’s forecast is higher than the 77% growth analysts estimate, according to LSEG data. Su told analysts that 80% of sales next year will come from data-center chips that will "drive the majority of our revenue and earnings growth." "We see demand across the data-center business, across our CPU business, as well as our data-center AI business," Su said. "And when you look at the rate and pace of that growth, we’ve been planning for it for the last several years." Data-center revenue jumped 97% to a record $8.55 billion in the third quarter, exceeding estimates of $8.20 billion. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of about $17 billion, plus or minus 3%, above analysts’ average estimate of $16.23 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. ...
